title: Study on Deep Nitrogen Removal Mechanisms in Mixotrophic Systems
description: Mixotrophic denitrification has great advantages in treating wastewater with a low carbon-to-nitrogen ratio. It can make full use of the carbon sources in the raw water, reducing the cost and carbon emissions associated with adding extra carbon. However, the boundary conditions and microscopic mechanisms of mixotrophic denitrification are still unclear. In this study, we explored the nitrogen removal characteristics of a mixotrophic nitrogen removal process under different autotrophic/heterotrophic denitrification ratios and found that the nitrogen removal performance of the mixotrophic reactor was best when the C/S ratio was 1:1. To understand the coupling mechanisms under this cultivation condition, we conducted microbial community and metagenomic analyses.
